title: Text-to-Speech (TTS) — From Tacotron to F5 and Kokoro

questions.question: What phonemes does phonemize("the") return?
options: ["the"]
questions.explanation: The longest-match loop sees the three-letter G2P entry the before trying shorter graphemes.

questions.question: What duration does duration(["AH"], jitter=0, seed=0) return?
questions.explanation: DURATION_FRAMES assigns AH a base of six frames and zero jitter leaves it unchanged.

questions.question: For phones=["AH","B"] and durs=[2,3], what total does mel_schedule(..., hop_ms=12.5) return?
options: 25 ms
5 ms

questions.question: What happens to an unknown phoneme in duration?
options: It is replaced with the sentence pause
It is removed from the phone sequence
It receives zero frames
It receives the fallback base duration of five frames
questions.explanation: DURATION_FRAMES.get(p, 5) supplies five frames when a symbol is absent.

questions.question: What does mel_schedule return for each phone?
options: The phone plus its start and end time in milliseconds
A waveform sample for every phoneme
A vocabulary index and speaker embedding
Only the total number of phones
questions.explanation: Each tuple is (p, t, t + d*hop_ms), and the function also returns the final time.

questions.question: Why is the duration schedule important before a FastSpeech-style vocoder?
options: It decides which microphone channel contains speech
It expands each phoneme into a predicted number of mel frames
It converts every word directly into a WAV header
It removes pauses so all utterances have equal length
questions.explanation: A duration model determines how long each phoneme occupies the acoustic frame sequence.
